context: a letter from J. D. Hooker, which you are answering
exchanges:
I arrived last Monday, having left my wife at Hitcham— all were well & cheerful there—when I left— Old Henslow was very much cut up, though being wondrous stolid he did not show it much & he, in common with all the family, occupied themselves throughout industriously. Poor Mrs. H went off as peacefully as possible,—without a struggle, having had no pain for the last 12 hours.— She was a very gentle lady, who I had become very deeply attached to of late years. She inherited the calm self-possession of the Jenyns to the full; had long known that any severe attack would certainly carry her off, & had led that kind of life which regarded death as going out of one room into another—happy soul!

Henslow was most sincerely pleased with the letters of his friends on the occasion, & I need not say with your’s as much as any— all spoke lovingly of her, as you did. too, & the old gentleman was always repeating that.
Thank you very much for note just received telling me all I wanted to know about the Henslows— Thanks.—
